cards.text: Solomon is king of Israel, and people are TALKING. The queen of Sheba hears about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD. And friend, she doesn't just nod and move on.

cards.question: The queen of Sheba has heard all about Solomon's fame. Why does she come to see him?

answers.text: To test him with hard questions
To end a war between them

cards.text: She rolls into Jerusalem with a very large caravan, camels loaded DOWN. Me? I came out of a clearance bin with a 25 cent sticker on me.

cards.question: What are the queen of Sheba's camels carrying into Jerusalem?

answers.text: Spices and gold and precious stones
Wool and bronze and fine linen

cards.text: Then she sits down with Solomon and tells him everything that's on her mind. Every hard question she brought, right there on the table.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon runs into a question from the queen of Sheba that's too difficult for him to explain.

cards.text: Then she sees it all: his wisdom, the palace he built, the food at his table, his servants and attendants, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presents at the house of the LORD.

cards.question: After seeing Solomon's wisdom, his palace and his whole court, how does the queen of Sheba react?

answers.text: She finds it a bit much

cards.text: She tells the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true." Friend, that's checking into a hotel and finding out the pictures online were HONEST.

cards.question: True or false: The queen of Sheba believed the report about Solomon before she came and saw it with her own eyes.
Now that she's seen it, how much of the real thing does the queen of Sheba say the report told her?

cards.text: Then she says, "How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!" I think she'd trade places with the STAFF in a heartbeat.

cards.question: Next the queen of Sheba says someone else is blessed too. Who?
The queen of Sheba says that because of the LORD's eternal love for Israel, He made Solomon king to carry out ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then she hands the king her gifts: 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones.

cards.question: True or false: After the queen of Sheba's gift, spices never again came in to Solomon in such abundance as hers.

cards.text: Quick side note in the text. Hiram king of Tyre has a fleet bringing gold from Ophir, and it also hauls in a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.

cards.question: What does Solomon make out of the almug wood Hiram's fleet brings in?

cards.text: King Solomon gives the queen of Sheba whatever she asks for, plus gifts out of his royal bounty, and she heads home with her servants. WHATEVER she asks, friend, and he means it.
Now the writer opens the books: 666 talents of gold come to Solomon each year. Friend, the Millers got ME for a quarter.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon's 666 talents of gold a year already include what the merchants, traders and Arabian kings bring him.

cards.text: So what does he do with all that gold? Shields: two hundred large ones and three hundred small ones, all hammered gold.

cards.question: Where does Solomon put the three hundred small gold shields?

answers.text: In the House of the Forest of Lebanon
In the house of the LORD

cards.text: Then comes the throne: a great throne of ivory overlaid with pure gold, with six steps, a rounded top and armrests on both sides.

cards.question: What stands beside each armrest of Solomon's throne, and at either end of each of its six steps?

cards.text: Twelve lions on the steps, and nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom. And here I am, thinking my little gold base is FANCY.

cards.question: All of Solomon's drinking cups are gold. In his days, ___ is accounted as nothing.

cards.text: Out on the water, Solomon has the ships of Tarshish sailing with Hiram's fleet. And friend, wait till you hear what they haul home.

cards.question: How often do the ships of Tarshish come back carrying gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks?
True or false: King Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

cards.text: The queen of Sheba was just the start. The whole world seeks an audience with Solomon to hear his wisdom.

cards.question: The whole world comes to hear Solomon's wisdom. Where did that wisdom come from?

answers.text: God put it in his heart
The queen of Sheba taught him

cards.question: Year after year, what does each visitor bring Solomon as tribute?

cards.text: Solomon gathers 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses and stations them in the chariot cities and with him in Jerusalem. Twelve THOUSAND horses, friend, and you thought finding parking downtown was rough.

cards.question: In Jerusalem, King Solomon makes silver as common as ___.

cards.text: Solomon's horses come in from Egypt and Kue, with a chariot from Egypt costing six hundred shekels of silver and a horse a hundred fifty. Then they're sent on to the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

findings.problem: The hotel joke treats the queen's words as a surprise that the pictures were honest. That suggests she doubted the report, which gives away the answer to card 10 (she did not believe it until she came and saw, 1 Kings 10:7).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The two-blank card asks the baker to put justice and righteousness in the exact BSB order. Whether a word goes in blank 1 or blank 2 depends on wording the baker hasn't seen, not on meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card calls Hiram "king of Tyre," which comes from outside the passage (for example 1 Kings 5:1). The card cites only 1 Kings 10:11, which does not say Tyre.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The closing line "WHATEVER she asks, friend, and he means it" just repeats the fact louder. It isn't a joke and reads like a pleasant filler line.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Verses 14-22 and 25-29 are an inventory of Solomon's wealth: yearly gold, shields, the throne, cups, the ships' cargo, tribute, chariots and the horse trade. That is mostly detail, with little happening. Stop 2 goes through it item by item and gives the details their own choice cards: where the shields go (card 4), the lions (card 6), the silver (card 8), how often the ships come (card 10) and what the tribute is (card 14). Only verses 23-24 carry the meaning of the stretch.

rule.text: If a stretch is mostly detail and not much happens, it counts.

findings.problem: The setup teases the cargo ("wait till you hear what they haul home"), but the next question lists the cargo and asks how often the ships come. The question doesn't come out of the moment Papa Dorin set up.

rule.text: The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: "The queen of Sheba was just the start" adds a fact: that she came first and the other visitors came after her. Verse 24 does not say this.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.
